messages:
laura_cs: FYI - Meridian reported a sudden drop in rerank quality after we pushed the latest quantization profile to their Dedicated cluster.
meridian-customer: Hi, our support ticket is CS-6789. Queries that used to return relevant docs now surface unrelated results. This started ~2026-03-07 09:10 UTC after the maintenance window.
laura_cs: attaching the two example queries they sent and the top-5 IDs. small repro below.
meridian-customer: Query: \"how to reset device firmware\"\nExpected top1: doc_112\nObserved top1: doc_87\nWe see lots of short irrelevant docs ranked above deep how-to guides.
sam_se: thanks — can you confirm whether you reindexed after the quant change? and which recall / rerank flow: ANN -> rerank(model) or hybrid?
meridian-customer: We didn't reindex. Flow: ANN (faiss, ivf_pq) -> server-side rerank with redwood-reranker-v1. ANN index uses quantized vectors (8-bit PQ) from the recent job.
mike_product: tagging eng — is this likely caused by PQ change + reranker sensitivity? Do we have metrics showing retrieval recall drop vs just rerank scoring drift?
jen_eng: initial hypothesis: PQ increased L2 distortion for long how-to docs, so ANN is not bringing the right candidates into reranked set. Reranker sees mostly shallow docs, so scores wrong. Need recall@100 delta.
laura_cs: Meridian provided a small eval set (50 queries). I uploaded it to /internal/cs/meridian/meridian_eval_50.json and linked the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-6789
jen_eng: quick local command to reproduce their metric:\n```\npython tools/eval_rerank.py --dataset /internal/cs/meridian/meridian_eval_50.json --ann-index /mnt/meridian/ann_ivfpq_8bit --reranker redwood-reranker-v1 --k 100 --metric mrr@10\n```
jen_eng: ran it on staging and saw mrr@10 drop from 0.42 -> 0.26 when using the 8-bit PQ index vs float baseline. so ANN recall loss is real.
mike_product: good data. two possible scopes: 1) quick mitigation: rollback quant profile or switch Meridian to float index (fast but costs more) 2) longer-term: improve PQ config + retrain/reindex + tune reranker to be robust to PQ noise.
laura_cs: Meridian is on a committed Dedicated contract and very sensitive to relevance. They want a short-term fix while we work on a durable solution.
jen_eng: rollback path: we can restore the previous float index snapshot from nightly backups. Reindex from scratch would take ~6-8 hours on their cluster; restore from snapshot ~45min + warming.
oncall-bot: Scheduled snapshot restore job created: job_id=restore-1972-01, eta ~45m. Ops will monitor CPU/GPU i/o. :gear:
mike_product: let's propose plan to customer: immediate restore of previous float index (opt-out of PQ) + product ticket to track PQ tuning + test harness to evaluate PQ impact on recall before future rollouts.
meridian-customer: we approve the restore. please proceed, we need notice before cutover and a POST rollback test run.
laura_cs: noted. I'm scheduling the restore window and will run the eval set after restore. I'll post results here.
jen_eng: post-restore checklist: 1) run eval_rerank on restored index 2) run A/B compare to PQ index for 24h 3) create PQ tuning job to test different PQ bytes on subset.
mike_product: I'll open a product backlog item: RB-1592 with scope: "PQ rollout safety: preflight eval harness + rollback automation + per-customer opt-out policy" and link CS-6789. Priority: P1 for Meridian (enterprise SLA).
laura_cs: added to ticket comments and cc'd Meridian. we'll mark this triage as customer-impacting and schedule quick postmortem after restore.
meridian-customer: thanks team. appreciated the fast response.
laura_cs: updating timeline: restore start 1972102800, expected done 1972103180. I'll post final mrr numbers after done.
jen_eng: follow-up action for eng: add recall@K monitoring to the rollout checklist and include synthetic queries mimicking long how-to docs.
mike_product: agree. also add rollout guard: if eval mrr@10 drop > 0.05, block auto-rollout and require manual approval.
laura_cs: closing immediate loop — will post results here when restore completes. :thumbsup:
